summary: Holiday non-bastard story on American folk singer Woody Guthrie, from Dust Bowl migrant radio star in 1930s California to Communist-aligned protest songwriter, wartime merchant mariner and blacklisted artist who died of Huntington's disease in 1967.
keywords: The Ballad of Pretty Boy Floyd

evidence.note: Guthrie leaves Texas for California in 1936; this part opens there
Depression work camps and Hoovervilles where he busks for migrant workers
segment on his racist on-air material and cartoons and his later apology
long segment on Pretty Boy Floyd, his crimes and the Robin Hood legend
Floyd's criminal career traced from his first arrest at about 18 to his 1934 death
follows the Communist line on the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact and Soviet invasions
Merchant Marine service, three torpedoed ships, drafted on VE Day
postwar Red Scare hearings and blacklisting
Huntington's onset late 1940s; obscenity charge in 1949
dies October 1967 after years in institutions

notes: Only Part Two is in the feed, so this story starts in 1936 and never covers his 1912 birth or childhood (Part One). I set partial_life for that reason, not because of how the story is framed. covered_span starts in about 1922 with the Floyd segment. Not used: Huntington's (no theme fits) and his sexually harassing letters, which get about 5 minutes; sexual-abuse could be added. The 'hero' format follows the 'non-bastard' wording in the description.
